How it works

You send a photo

Submit a few high-resolution photos of your pet, choose your preferred size and style, and then I go to the drawing board. 50% is due upfront, and 50% is due when your piece has been delivered. :)

See Prices
I draw

I create a drawing of your pet(s), typically done in charcoal and pencil. Your custom art, official Donor Card, and a special gift will be mailed to you, or you may pick them up. Framing assistance available.

See Gallery
I donate 50%

50% of funds are donated to local or national, highly-rated rescues, undercover welfare agencies, wildlife protection, and ethical science programs. Or you may choose an animal charity that’s close to your heart.

Donation recipients

50% of proceeds are donated to local or national, highly-rated rescues, shelters, wildlife conservation, or anti-testing programs. All of the recipients have high ratings on Charity Navigator and/or are organizations that I work with and trust. These organizations help factory farmed animals, abused animals from dog-fighting rings and puppy mills, animals who’ve been mistreated or abandoned by their parent, dog meat festival rescues, shelter medical centers, wildlife stolen from their families and tested on or made to perform for us, or animals being poached for their body parts, and more.

  • (ARM) Animal Recovery Mission
  • Broken Shovels Farm Sanctuary
  • Center for Ethical Science
  • CPR K9 Fund Chicago Rescue
  • Denver Conservation Alliance
  • Evergreen Animal Protection League
  • Farm Sanctuary (New York)
  • Hoedspruit Endangered Species Centre

About the Cause

Art that
gives back

shelter
food
love
freedom

AFA is a small, woman-owned business whose mission is to get the community involved in giving to animal organizations and to help honor pets through art. I draw a custom sketch of your pet(s), and 50% of the proceeds go to support local or national, highly-rated rescues, wildlife, and ethical science programs. All of the donation recipients have high ratings on Charity Navigator and/or I’ve worked with them personally and fully trust the integrity of the organization. You may also choose an animal organization that’s close to your heart.

You’ll feel great knowing you’ve given mistreated animals shelter, food, love, and freedom from their nightmare, you’ll have a piece of art to honor your pet forever, and animals all over the world are saved.

Everyone wins!
My Story

Was I the
good guy?

In the movies, it’s easy to spot the good guy and the bad guy. In real life, most of us assume we’re the good guy, and that the harm is coming from someone else. But so much of the hurt in the world comes from people thinking “it’s not me” or “one person doesn’t matter.” As the late, great Jane Goodall reminded us: that’s 8 billion people, all doing nothing. The small things we do, or don’t do, every day add up, for our planet and for animals, and we often don’t see it until it’s too late.

When that realization hit me, I had to ask myself: Am I the good guy, or the one who does nothing? Will I be proud of how I lived? Those questions changed everything. I couldn’t look away anymore. It was time to get off my butt and do something. If one butterfly can change the direction of the wind, surely I can make a difference.

Keep reading

So I changed how I live. By 2015, I’d spent a year living as a vegan (despite my love of cheese), protesting, petitioning, donating, and volunteering, both locally and overseas. It still didn’t feel like enough. The rescues I work with need real financial help, while their people work tirelessly for little or no pay. I also wanted to give others who care a new way to help their fellow Earthlings. So I put my pencil to work, and Art for Animals was born.

If it troubles you that animals suffer, you’re not alone. From factory farms and fighting rings to breeding mills, abandonment, animal testing and poaching, it happens every day, all over the world. But there’s hope. It’s a challenge we can overcome, together, one portrait at a time. What a happy world it is when we can make a difference just by making pretty things together.

Always a friend, Theresa
